# Unreleased

Staging note for the next release. Fold it into that release's `<tag>.md` (the release job reads `.github/release-notes/<tag>.md`) and delete this file.

## New

- **Drag files, folders, images and text into the chat input.** A workspace file dropped from the VS Code Explorer or an editor tab becomes an `@` file chip (read when you send, as if picked from the `@` list); a folder becomes an `@` folder chip, which is a search scope rather than the folder's whole contents. Images go through the image attachment (only for models that read images; at most 10 per message, 5 MB each), dropped text loses hidden characters, and a link is added as text without being fetched. Files that look like they hold secrets (`.env` files, keys and certificates, `.ssh` and cloud credential folders), files outside the workspace, and files from the operating system's file manager other than images are refused, and the input says which file and why; a refused file is never read. In VS Code, hold Shift while dragging. VS Code 1.140 and later stop Explorer and tab drops from reaching extension webviews (microsoft/vscode#339036); until VS Code fixes that, use `@` for workspace files. JetBrains IDEs are reported not to deliver drops to the chat (its browser is off-screen); use `@` there.
- **A price for any model, so dollar budgets work on local and unlisted models.** Add `pricing:` to a model in config.yaml: `input` and `output` (required), and optionally `cacheRead` and `cacheWrite`, in US dollars per million tokens (`currency: USD` may be written; no other currency is accepted). Zero is a real price, for a model on your own hardware. A model with a price is no longer refused by `--max-budget-usd`: the run's spend and the estimate before each request use it, ahead of any price table, and the budget's price note says "your config". Cache rates left out are priced at the input rate. The **Configure** dialog's Context & cost tab has the four fields and shows the price with its source.
- **The model Configure dialog has two more tabs and the remaining provider settings.** **Templates & system message**: the chat, agent and plan system messages (the built-in text is shown greyed until you type your own, with a preview per mode), the chat template with a preview of the prompt it builds (or a note that the provider applies the model's own template), the edit, apply and autocomplete prompt templates rendered with sample values (a template that does not compile, or reads a variable that is never filled in, is flagged), and per-tool overrides (a different description, or the tool turned off for this model) with a preview of what the model gets. **Advanced (YAML)**: the model's entry as written, comments included, credentials masked; an edit there is reviewed and saved like the other tabs (the same diff, the same check that the file did not change meanwhile), only the settings the dialog manages can change, and a setting changed both there and on another tab is refused rather than one silently winning. **Connection** now also has Bedrock's service tier, latency mode, guardrail id and version, and cross-region inference; the AWS access key id, secret access key and session token (stored as secrets, never written into config.yaml); and the watsonx deployment id, project id and API version. Tab and Shift+Tab now stay inside the dialog, and closing it returns focus to the control that opened it.
